questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the flow of energy between various components of the environment?

options.text: The amount of organic matter present at each trophic level is 10%.
Green plants capture about 10% of the solar energy that falls on leaves.
Every trophic level loses some energy as heat to the environment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Green plants capture about 10% of the solar energy that falls on leaves__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Plants absorb **only 1-2% **of the **sunlight **that falls on leaves, as **98-99 % of the sunlight **is **reflected back** and converted to heat.
 
• Energy flow is **unidirectional** from the lower trophic level to the higher trophic level. 
 
• **10%** of energy is absorbed by each trophic level and the rest is lost in the environment.

questions.question: The association of algae and fungi for the formation of lichens is an example of
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• A habitat always has more than one species, which interact with the environment as well as among themselves.
 
• These interactions help in forming a functional biotic community.
 
• The interactions can be:
 
 
• **Intraspecific** - takes place among the individuals of the same species.
 
• **Interspecific** - takes place among populations of two different species.
 
 
 
• Based of their effects, the **interspecific interactions** can be of 3 types:
 
 
• **Beneficial** - These are positive interactions where either one or both of the species are benefitted.
 
• **Detrimental** - These are the negative interactions where one or both of the species are harmed.
 
• **Neutral** - These are interactions where the species is not affected.
 
 
 
• It is important to note here that an interaction that is beneficial to one species may or may not be beneficial to the other species.

**Major Types of Interactions**:

 Note:

 '+' : Beneficial

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mutualism** is a type of interaction in which **both the species is benefitted**.
 
• A lichen is formed as a result of **symbiotic association between an algae and a fungi**.
 
• Symbiosis is essentially a mutualistic interaction.
 
• The fungal component is called **mycobiont** and the algal component is called **photobiont**.
 
• The **mycobiont** produces a thallus structure that contains and **protects the photobiont**.
 
• The **photobiont** performs the **photosynthetic** functions for the lichen.

Therefore, **the association of algae and fungi for the formation of lichens is an example of mutualism**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a biotic component of the ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil** is an abiotic component of the ecosystem.
 
• Biotic components refer to the living parts of an ecosystem, such as **frogs, flowers, and insects**.
 
• Abiotic components are the non-living parts of an ecosystem that influence living organisms, including **soil, water, and air**.
 
• Soil provides essential nutrients and a medium for plant growth, but it itself is not a living entity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An ecosystem consists of both **biotic** (living) and **abiotic** (non-living) components that interact with each other.
 
• Examples of biotic components include **plants, animals, bacteria, and fungi**.
 
• Abiotic components include **climate, sunlight, temperature, and soil**.
 
• Understanding the distinction between biotic and abiotic components is essential for studying ecological interactions and environmental science.

questions.question: Which of the following trophic levels (in the pyramid of number) has maximum number of individuals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Producers.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Producers** are the **base of the food chain** and support all other trophic levels.
 
• They are the organisms that can **make their own food** through the process of **photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.**
 
• Therefore, they have the **highest number of individuals** in the pyramid of numbers.
 
• Producers are also known as** autotrophs**, which means **"self-feeders**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary consumers **are the** herbivores** that **eat producers.**

 
 
• They have **fewer individuals** than producers because they need to consume a** larger quantity of producers** to meet their energy requirements.
 
 
 
• **Secondary consumers **are the **carnivores** that **eat herbivores.**
 
 
• They have **even fewer individuals** than primary consumers because they need to consume a** larger quantity of primary consumers** to meet their energy requirements. 
 
 
 
• **Tertiary consumers** are the** top predators** that **eat other carnivores.**
 
 
• They have the** fewest individuals** in the pyramid of numbers because they need to consume a larger quantity of secondary consumers to meet their energy requirements.

questions.question: Which biotic component of an ecosystem is present in the greatest number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Producers**__.

**Note:** As per the official answer key, the correct answer is** Tertiary Consumers **but in actual the correct answer would be **Producers** because producers form the base of the ecological pyramid. As they are the primary source of energy for all other organisms in the ecosystem, producers are the most abundant biotic component.

**Source: ** https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebo114.pdf

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Producers** are the organisms in an ecosystem that produce energy-rich compounds like glucose through photosynthesis.
 
• They form the base of the food chain and are critical for energy flow in an ecosystem.
 
• Examples of producers include **plants, algae, and cyanobacteria**.
 
• Producers convert sunlight into chemical energy, which is utilized by all other biotic components.
 
• Their large numbers are essential for supporting the energy needs of the entire ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Consumers**

 
 
• These organisms, also called herbivores, feed directly on producers.
 
• Examples include cows, deer, and caterpillars.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Consumers**
 
 
• These are carnivores or omnivores that feed on primary consumers.
 
• Examples include frogs, small birds, and some fish.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**
 
 
• These are apex predators that consume secondary consumers.
 
• Examples include lions, eagles, and sharks.

questions.question: The concept of ecological pyramids was introduced by:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Ecological pyramids **are the graphical representation of the organisms that belong to **successive trophic levels**. 
 
• The comparison between the different trophic levels is with respect to **energy, biomass and number**.
 
• An ecological pyramid comprises a **broader base **that represents the **producers or the first trophic level.**
 
• The pyramid gradually **narrows upwards** forming an **inverted cone** structure. The **apex** represents the **top-level consumer**.
 
• There are three types of ecological pyramids:

 
• Pyramid of number
 
• Pyramid of biomass
 
• Pyramid of energy

 
• A **well-balanced ecosystem** shows an **upright pyramid of numbers, biomass and energy. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2610577c9444526d7a1e45391b5f0d742065eced2790293301a64ac7ab023def.png] ​

**Explanation:**__

 
• **Option 1: Tansley - INCORRECT**

 
 
• **​**Sir Arthur George Tansley was an English botanist.
 
• He coined the term **'ecosystem'.**
 
• According to Tansley, the ecosystem is the integration of the biotic community and its physical environment and it is the fundamental unit of ecology.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Elton - CORRECT**
 
 
• Charles Elton was an English biologist. 
 
• He has framed the basic principles of animal ecology.
 
• The **idea of the ecological pyramid **was first presented by Charles Elton in 1939.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Odum - INCORRECT**
 
 
• Eugene Odum was an American biologist.
 
• He is known for his work on ecosystem ecology.
 
• Eugene Odum along with his brother Howard Odum wrote the book ***Fundamentals of Ecology.***
 
 
 
• ***​*Option 4: Haeckel - INCORRECT**
 
 
• Ernst Haeckel was a German zoologist.
 
• The word **'ecology'** was coined by him.
 
 

 

**So the correct answer is option 2 (Elton).**

questions.question: Which of the following substances will take the longest time to degrade naturally in the environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leather**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Leather** is a material made from the hide or skin of animals, primarily cattle.
 
• It takes a significantly longer time to degrade in the environment compared to organic materials like leaves or paper.
 
• The degradation process of leather can take up to several decades, depending on the treatment and the environmental conditions.
 
• This prolonged degradation period is due to the tanning process, which stabilizes the collagen fibers in the hide and makes the leather resistant to biological attack.
 
• Leather is often treated with chemicals, which further slow down its decomposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Leaves**__

 __
 
• **Leaves** are organic materials that decompose relatively quickly.
 
• The decomposition process usually takes a few weeks to a few months.
 
• Leaves are rich in nutrients, which aids in their quick breakdown by microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Paper**__
 __
 
• **Paper** is primarily composed of cellulose fibers and is biodegradable.
 
• It typically takes a few weeks to months to degrade, depending on environmental conditions.
 
• Recycling and composting are common methods to manage paper waste.
 
 
 
• **Cardboard box**__
 
 
• Like paper, **cardboard** is made from cellulose fibers and is biodegradable.
 
• Cardboard boxes decompose in a few months under the right conditions.
 
• They are often recycled or composted to reduce environmental impact.

questions.question: Which of the following factors exclusively affects reproduction in seasonal breeders, both plants and animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Photoperiod__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Photoperiod** is an important concept in biology related to the **activity and behavior of organisms** based on **length of day and night**.
 
• **Photoperiod **refers to the **relative length of day and night**, and it is a** key environmental cue** that **many plants and animals **use to regulate their **physiological processes**.
 
• **Photoperiodism **is the **response of organisms, especially plants, to the photoperiod**, which can influence processes such as** flowering, dormancy, and growth**.
 
• For instance, some plants require **exposure to sunlight** for a** specific duration **to trigger flowering.
 
• Others may use the photoperiod to determine when to enter a **state of dormancy** for the winter.
 
• According to the photoperiod, plants are categorized into **short-day plants** (flower when day length is less than a critical length), **long-day plants** (flower when day length is longer than a critical length), and **day-neutral plants** (flower regardless of the day length).
 
• Beyond plants,** photoperiod can also affect animals**.
 
• Many** birds** use the photoperiod as a cue for** migratory behaviors**, while some **mammals** use it to time **reproductive cycles** or **hibernation periods**.
 
• Due to the** tilt of Earth's axis** and its** elliptical orbit around **the sun, the **photoperiod changes throughout the year**, which organisms use to regulate their** seasonal activities**.
